events.text: Mount Hua and Wudang have shared the Qinling border for three hundred years, and argued about where it runs for two hundred and ninety. This spring someone from the other mountain cuts down one of your sect's plum trees 'that was on the wrong side'. Your sect wants a reply.

choices.text: Volunteer to carry the sect's protest to the other mountain

effects.log: You carry a very polite letter down the mountain. Nobody expects it to work.

choices.text: Suggest the plum tree was, in fact, on the wrong side

effects.log: The elders look at you as if you had cut it down yourself. The letter goes without you.

events.text: The border quarrel has become a border war. Disciples of the other mountain and your sect's meet on the ridge path with blades drawn, and you are among them.

ok.log: Steel on the ridge. The plum trees watch.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Plum Tree Border

choices.text: Step between the lines and talk

effects.log: You stand in the middle with your arms out. Somebody laughs. Then, slowly, everybody does.

events.text: The Alliance calls both sects to a summit at Luoyang. Your name is on the list of those who were on the ridge that day, and the Alliance Leader asks for your account.

choices.text: Tell it plainly, faults on both sides

effects.log: The hall is quiet. Then the Alliance Leader nods, and the border is drawn where it always should have been.

choices.text: Tell it the way your sect wants it told

effects.log: Your sect wins the border and loses the room. The other mountain remembers.

events.arc: The Night of the Red Sashes
events.text: Charcoal burners come down from the hills with a story: men in black with red sashes, camped in the old quarry, counting the paths to your gate.

choices.text: Report it to the elders at once

effects.log: The elders double the gate watch. The quarry is empty by the time anyone looks, which worries them more.
You lie in the ferns above the quarry and count forty men. One of them looks straight at your hiding place and smiles.

events.arc: The Night of the Red Sashes
events.text: They come on the night of the new moon. Fire in the outer halls, screaming in the dormitories, and a man in a red sash at the end of your corridor.

ok.log: Your blade meets his in the smoke.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Night of the Red Sashes

choices.text: Get the youngest disciples out first

effects.log: You carry two children through the burning kitchen and go back for a third. The Cult does not follow you into the fire.

events.arc: The Night of the Red Sashes
events.text: Your people count their dead and rebuild their halls. The master of the house names a party to carry the war back to the Cult's quarry camp, and asks who will go.

ok.log: A dawn raid of your own. The red sashes do not expect it.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Night of the Red Sashes

effects.log: Someone has to raise the halls again. Years later the new dormitory is called by your name, which embarrasses you.

events.arc: The Night of the Red Sashes
events.text: A letter, years on, in a careful hand: the Cult captain who led the raid is old now, and sick, and asks to see one of the disciples he fought that night before he dies.

effects.log: He is a small old man in a mountain hut. He apologises for nothing and thanks you for coming. You do not understand it, and you are glad you went.
You burn the letter. Some doors are better left shut.

events.text: A Greenwood stronghold has put a chain across the mountain road and a toll on every cart. The merchants of the town come to you, because you are the only martial artist they know who is not already on the bandits' payroll.

choices.text: Take their silver and clear the road

ok.log: Forty taels up front. You walk up the road alone, which the bandits find hilarious.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Chain Across the Road

choices.text: Refuse: this is the magistrate's problem

effects.log: The magistrate's problem stays the merchants' problem. The toll rises.

events.text: The stronghold's lieutenant finds you at the inn, unarmed, with wine. 'You fight well. The chief pays better than merchants, and we do not make you carry anything.'

effects.log: He shrugs, pays for the wine, and leaves. You have made a polite enemy.
You are a bandit now, or near enough. The road pays you instead of the merchants.

events.text: The Greenwood King himself rides through the province to settle the stronghold's quarrel with the road. He has heard your name, and summons you to the fort.

choices.text: Go, and speak for the merchants

effects.log: The King listens for a long time and then names a toll a cart can actually pay. The merchants call it a miracle. The lieutenant calls it your fault.

choices.text: Go, and challenge the lieutenant before the King

ok.log: A duel in the fort's yard, the King watching from his chair.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Chain Across the Road

events.text: The Water Gang's whistle sounds on the docks and every porter stops. A rival gang has taken the lower pier, and the great river is about to be fought over with boathooks.

effects.log: You watch from the teahouse as the docks burn a little.

choices.text: Help the porters hold the upper pier

ok.log: Boathooks and oars in the dark. You are on the winning pier by dawn.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of War on the Piers

events.text: The ferry you are on is boarded mid-river by the losing gang, looking for anyone who stood on the upper pier. They have your description.

ok.log: A narrow deck, a wide river.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of War on the Piers

effects.log: The river is cold and fast and takes you two li downstream. You lose your boots and keep your life.

events.text: The Lord of the Water Gang invites you to his junk, lanterns on the water, a table of river fish. He would like the two gangs' war to end and thinks you could carry the terms.

effects.log: You row between two angry junks for three nights. On the fourth the river is quiet.

choices.text: Ask what is in it for you

effects.log: He laughs and names a sum. It is a good sum. The war ends anyway.

events.text: The Beggar King is dead, found peaceful under a bridge with his dog beside him. By nightfall the Sect has two Kings, one from the Dirty Robes and one from the Clean Robes, and both want your bowl on their side.

choices.text: The Dirty Robes: the old way

effects.log: You stand with the ones who still beg.

choices.text: The Clean Robes: the Sect should own inns, not bowls

effects.log: You stand with the ones who count silver.

events.text: The two Kings agree to settle it the Sect's way: a Green Bamboo Staff contest on the riverbank, each side's best. Yours is sick. They hand you the staff.

ok.log: Staff against staff on the mud.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Two Kings Under One Bridge

choices.text: Break the staff over your knee and tell them both to grow up

effects.log: Silence. Then the old beggars begin to laugh, and the Sect has one King again by morning, and it is neither of them.

events.text: The new Beggar King, years on, is dying under the same bridge, and names you. The whole Sect is watching to see if you will take the staff.

effects.log: You are the Beggar King. It comes with a dog.
You hand the staff on. The Sect will say you were wise. The dog follows you anyway.

events.text: A village well on the Sichuan road turns black and three families die. The cup left on the well's rim bears the mark of your sect's rivals, which is either proof or exactly what a clever poisoner would leave.

effects.log: You follow the trade in bitter roots from market to market.
Two more families live because you brewed before you hunted.

events.text: An envoy from the rival house meets you at a teahouse with a proposal: a duel of antidotes. Each side's best poisoner, each drinks the other's cup, and the first to stand without help wins the quarrel.

effects.log: The cup is bitter and the room goes grey. You stand first, barely.

choices.text: Refuse, and name the real poisoner

effects.log: You lay the roots on the table and the trail that led to them. The envoy goes white. It was one of theirs, and not on their orders.

events.text: A truce between the houses, signed in a tent between two mountains. Your name is on it as witness, and the rival's patriarch leaves you a small lacquered box.

effects.log: A recipe, written small: the antidote to their house's deadliest work. A gift, or a message.
The patriarch bows a little lower than a patriarch should. You have made a friend you will never see again.

events.text: Heralds ride to every orthodox sect: the Martial Alliance will choose a new Leader at the summit in Luoyang this autumn, and your name is on the list of those invited to attend.

effects.log: The great hall of the Alliance, banners of every sect, and more knives than the kitchen needs.
You stay home. The summit happens without you, which is how most summits happen.

events.text: Three candidates, and one of them has a sect brother in the kitchens. Someone slips a vial into the candidates' wine. You see it done.

choices.text: Knock the cups from the table

ok.log: Wine on the Alliance floor and a dagger drawn in the kitchen door.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Summit at Luoyang

choices.text: Say nothing and watch who drinks

effects.log: One candidate falls. The other two look at each other, and then at you. You have learned something and lost something.

events.text: The vote. The surviving candidates are tied, and by the Alliance's old rule the tie is broken by whoever the hall names as its witness of honour. The hall names you.

effects.log: A hard Leader for hard years. The sects grumble and obey.
A gentle Leader. Trade flourishes and the Cult sharpens its knives.

events.text: Years later the Leader you helped choose sends for you. The seat is heavy, and they would like the witness of honour to say, honestly, whether they have earned it.

effects.log: They weep, a little, which Leaders are not supposed to do. You are given a jade token that opens every Alliance door.
They listen to all of it. The next year's decrees are better.

events.text: A village on the road has no smoke from its chimneys. Inside, every bed is made and every well is red. The old men of the next village whisper a name no one has said in a century.

effects.log: Bare footprints in the ash lead into the hills. Many of them. All of them small.
The Alliance sends a company. By the time it arrives there are two more empty villages.

events.text: The Blood Cult's altar is in a cave behind a waterfall, lit by candles made of something you do not look at closely. Their puppets stand in rows, and they are the villagers.

ok.log: The puppets do not bleed. The priests do.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Empty Villages

choices.text: Bring the mountain down on the cave

effects.log: You spend a day working the ledge above the falls loose, and the cave is gone under stone by night. So are the villagers. You tell no one that part.

events.text: The war is over and the sects count the credit. A Blood Cult priest, caught alive, claims under questioning that you made a bargain at the altar. Three elders believe him.

choices.text: Demand a trial before the Alliance

effects.log: You stand in the hall and tell what happened. The priest's story falls apart in an hour.

choices.text: Find the three elders and ask them why

ok.log: One of them took the Cult's silver. He does not survive the asking.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Empty Villages

events.text: {npc} says, loudly, in front of everyone, that the manual you learned your first form from was stolen from {his} family's shelf. {He} has no proof. {He} has a crowd.

choices.text: Spar, here and now, and let the form speak

ok.log: You fight in the dust until an elder pulls you apart. Nobody remembers the manual afterwards; everybody remembers the fight.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.

effects.log: {npc} is left shouting at your back. It costs you nothing today.

events.text: The tournament draw puts you against {npc} in the first round. {He} has trained for this for years. So, {he} says, have you, with {his} family's manual.

ok.log: The crowd knows the story. They lean in.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Stolen Manual

choices.text: Offer to fight with a borrowed, unfamiliar sabre

ok.log: You fight with a weapon you have never held, to prove the form was never the point. Win or lose, {npc} is quiet afterwards.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Stolen Manual

effects.log: You bow and step out of the ring before the first exchange. The crowd jeers. {npc} is left standing alone with {his} family's forms and nobody to show them to.

events.text: {npc}, grey now, finds you at a teahouse and puts a very old manual on the table between you. 'It was never stolen,' {he} says. 'My grandfather gave it to yours. I found the letter last year.'

effects.log: Two old people and a manual that was never stolen. You stay until the teahouse closes.
{He} laughs so hard the owner comes over. It is the start of a friendship long overdue.

events.text: One promotion, two disciples. {npc} is the other one, and {he} has begun arriving at the training yard before dawn to be seen there.

effects.log: You and {npc} greet each other at the yard in the dark for a season. The elders notice both of you.
Let {him} be seen. You get better.

events.text: The night before the trial, your practice blade is gone from the rack and {npc} was the last one in the yard. {He} swears {he} did not touch it.

effects.log: You fight the trial with a borrowed blade. {npc} watches from the wall with an expression you cannot read.
The blade turns up in another disciple's chest the next week. You were wrong, and everyone knows it.

events.text: Years on, an elder of the sect lies dying and the council must choose the next elder from two names. One is yours. One is {npc}'s.

effects.log: You tell the council {npc} is the better choice. They choose you anyway, and {npc} never forgets that you spoke.
You lay out your years and your merit. The council agrees. {npc} bows and leaves the mountain within the year.

events.text: There is someone at the Lantern Festival you cannot stop looking at. {npc} notices, because {npc} is looking at the same person.

effects.log: You win the conversation. {npc} wins the next festival's.
You watch from the bridge. The lantern you float says a name you do not say aloud.

events.text: The matter is settled the murim way: Your rival from the Lantern Festival challenges you under the plum trees, with {npc}, the one you both love, told to stay away and watching from the gate.

ok.log: Petals and steel.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Lantern Rival

choices.text: Refuse: a heart is not a prize

effects.log: You sheathe your blade and walk to the gate, and ask the question properly. The answer is yes, and there is a wedding when the plum trees bloom.

events.text: {npc}, years later, at your gate with a wedding gift that is very late and a bottle of very good wine.

choices.text: Open the gift, and put the kettle on

effects.log: You pour tea and raise your cup to the plum trees. {He} married well too, {he} says. You believe {him}.
'To stop hating you,' {he} says. 'It takes a lot of effort.' You pour.

events.text: {npc} has not been seen for a year. Then a village is found with every door marked in red, and the sect brother who survived swears the blade was {npc}'s.

effects.log: You follow red doors across two provinces.
You tell the elders {npc} would never. Someone else is sent.

events.text: A ruined temple in the rain, and {npc} on the altar steps with eyes gone dark. 'You came. I knew you would be the one.' {He} draws.

ok.log: The duel you both always knew was coming.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Red Doors

choices.text: Fight to disarm, and drag {him} home

ok.log: You break {his} sword arm and carry {him} down the mountain. {His} own sect locks {him} in the cold cells for three years. {He} comes out whole.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Red Doors

choices.text: Sheathe your sword and walk back into the rain

effects.log: You turn your back on {him}. {He} does not follow. Behind you, on the altar steps, {he} laughs for too long. Whatever {he} becomes now, you will hear of it from others.

events.text: A young fighter at your gate with {npc}'s eyes and {npc}'s stance, who has come either to thank you or to kill you, and has not decided which.

effects.log: They stay for three years and leave as your disciple.

choices.text: Tell them the whole story first

effects.log: They listen without moving. At the end they bow, and go, and you never learn which way they decided.

events.text: Your master has taken a second student, and the second student is better than you. {npc} does not pretend otherwise.

effects.log: Dawn and midnight, every day, for a year.
'Because you already know you are good,' {he} says, 'and the other one does not yet.' It is not the answer you wanted.

events.text: Your master sets the two of you the same test: the waterfall form, at the falls, at dawn, with {him} watching from the rocks.

ok.log: Water and steel. You finish; so does the other student.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Second Student

choices.text: Perform the form your own way

effects.log: You change the third movement. Your master says nothing for a long time, then: 'That is not my form.' Then: 'It is better.'

events.text: Your master's last illness. {He} calls you both to the bedside and holds out the sect seal with a hand that shakes.

effects.log: The seal is heavier than it looks. The other student bows to you first.

choices.text: Close your master's hand around it and call the other student forward

effects.log: You give up the seal. Your master watches you do it and smiles the smile you spent your youth trying to earn.

events.text: An ambush on the mountain road, four blades and yours already broken. Then {npc}, of all people, drops from the rocks above and stands beside you.

ok.log: Two people who cannot stand each other, fighting as if they had trained together all their lives.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Back to Back

ok.log: {He} does not run. Neither do you.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Back to Back

choices.text: Break for the trees while {he} holds them

effects.log: You run, and a blade opens your arm as you go. Behind you steel rings for a long time, then stops. Months later you hear {npc} lived, and tells the story of the road with you in it, running.

events.text: {npc} never mentions the road. {He} does, however, mention that {his} sect is going to war next spring and that the odds are not good.

ok.log: You fight under a banner that is not yours, for a person who would never ask.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Back to Back

effects.log: The silver buys {his} sect a hundred arrows. {He} writes to thank you, which must have hurt.
{He} nods as if {he} expected nothing else and leaves before the tea is cold. The debt from the mountain road stays between you, unpaid.

events.text: Your master coughs blood into a cloth and folds it away before you can see. You saw.

choices.text: Find a physician, whatever it costs

effects.log: The physician says a year, perhaps two. Your master says the physician is a fool, and starts putting the sect's affairs in order.
You pretend you saw nothing. {He} pretends to believe you. The training grows harder.

events.text: Three disciples, one seal. Your master sets a test nobody expected: carry water up the mountain for a month, and say nothing about it.

effects.log: Thirty days. Your shoulders change shape.

choices.text: Ask what water has to do with the sword

effects.log: 'Everything,' {he} says, and sends you back down for another bucket.

events.text: The seal, at last, on a quiet morning. {He} has chosen, and {he} has chosen you, and the other two disciples are standing right there.

effects.log: You are the heir. One of the other two leaves the mountain that night.

choices.text: Ask for a year to prove it

effects.log: Your master laughs, which brings on the coughing. 'A year, then.' {He} lives exactly that long.

events.text: The sect leader has not left the inner hall in a season. The elders meet without the leader, and the meeting is about who comes after.

effects.log: A silence, then a nod from the oldest elder. You are a candidate.
You throw your weight behind the obvious choice. It is remembered.

events.text: A purse of silver appears in your quarters with a note: the other candidate would be grateful for your withdrawal, and generous.

choices.text: Return the purse to the elders' table, in front of everyone

effects.log: The hall goes still. The other candidate's face does something complicated.
You are rich and no longer a candidate. The sect gets the leader it deserves.

events.text: The elders cannot agree, so the sect does it the old way: a duel in the yard before the whole mountain, first blood, for the seal.

ok.log: The yard, the banners, every disciple on the walls.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Who Comes After

choices.text: Propose the sect's first vote instead

effects.log: Every disciple drops a stone in a bowl. It takes all day. The sect has a leader by nightfall, and a new tradition.

events.text: Behind the loose brick in your master's study, a manual bound in red leather: a demonic art, written in {his} own hand, many years ago.

effects.log: The first page is enough to make your qi stir in a way it should not.

choices.text: Put it back and say nothing

effects.log: You replace the brick. You dream about the red leather for a month.

events.text: Your master knows. {He} always knew where every brick in that study sat. 'Now you know what I was,' {he} says. 'Ask what you want to ask.'

effects.log: 'Because of what it cost. Not me. Other people.' {He} tells you, all of it, until morning.

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach it to you

effects.log: {He} looks at you for a long time. 'No.' Then, quietly: 'Not yet.'

events.text: The red manual comes to you wrapped in oilcloth, with a letter in your old master's hand: burn it, or use it to do what I could not. The letter does not say which.

effects.log: Red leather curls in the brazier. Something in your chest unknots.
You hide it behind a brick of your own.

events.arc: The Old Man at the Gate
events.text: A stranger at the gate, old and poor, who says your master killed {his} whole family many years ago and walked away. {He} wants to say it to your master's face.

effects.log: The two old men look at each other for a long time. Your master does not deny it.
You turn an old man from the gate. It is the easiest thing you have ever done and you never stop thinking about it.

events.arc: The Old Man at the Gate
events.text: The story spreads. The sect's council summons your master, and {he} asks you to stand with {him}, or against {him}; {he} will understand either.

effects.log: You speak of the years since. The council listens. {He} keeps {his} seat and loses {his} name.
You tell the truth. {He} nods at every word. {He} leaves the mountain that night to find the old man, and does not return.

events.text: Your own sect has grown, and two of your disciples have begun to look at the seal on your table more than at you.

effects.log: You name the steadier one. The other's face closes like a door.
A mission that needs both of them. They come back friends, or one of them does not come back.

events.text: The passed-over disciple leaves in the night with a copy of your sect's first manual and three of the younger students.

effects.log: A second sect, with your forms and their name. In time people will argue about which is the true line.

ok.log: You catch them on the pass. The manual comes back. The students choose, and two choose you.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Your Own Heir

events.text: Your own last illness, and the heir you chose kneeling by the bed with the whole sect in the courtyard outside.

choices.text: Tell them the sect is theirs

effects.log: The seal changes hands. Outside, the disciples bow to a new master.

choices.text: Tell them the one thing you never told anyone

effects.log: A secret, a form, a name. They carry it out to the courtyard and the sect is stronger for it.

events.text: Men come to the door about your father's debt at the gambling house. Your father is not home. Your mother is.

effects.log: You are small and the men are not. One of them laughs, and then stops laughing.
The street fills with people. The men leave, promising to come back.

events.text: Your father's debt is called in: pay by the new year or the house is the gambling master's. The family has half of it.

choices.text: Work every job in town for a season

effects.log: You carry water, sweep the inn, hold horses. It is still not enough, until the innkeeper quietly adds the rest.

choices.text: Challenge the gambling master's bodyguard for the debt

ok.log: A fight for the house, in the gambling house's own yard.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Your Father's Debt

choices.text: Beg the gambling master for another year

effects.log: You kneel in the gambling house's yard until your knees bleed. The master laughs and grants the year, for the entertainment. The family keeps the house, and the whole town saw you kneel.

events.text: Your father, years later and sober for most of them, hands you a small heavy bag. It is the debt, repaid to you, a coin at a time, over many years.

effects.log: You keep the bag unopened on your shelf for the rest of your life.
'Buy something for the house,' you say. He does. It is a goat.

events.arc: The Red Sash in the Bag
events.text: {npc} comes home with a red sash in {his} bag. {He} has been meeting the Cult's recruiters at the edge of town for a season.

effects.log: {He} does not speak to you for a year. {He} does not go to the Cult either.
'Because they want me,' {he} says, 'and nobody else does.' You do not have an answer that night.

events.arc: The Red Sash in the Bag
events.text: A letter from the Hundred Thousand Mountains in {npc}'s hand: {he} is well, {he} is a Black Robe now, {he} is sorry, {he} is not sorry.

effects.log: You write every season. {He} answers every other one.
You tell your parents {he} is dead. It is easier. It is also a lie you will carry.

events.arc: The Red Sash in the Bag
events.text: On a battlefield between the sects and the Cult, a Black Robe lowers {his} blade and pulls off {his} mask. It is {npc}.

effects.log: You stand in the middle of a war and talk about your mother. Then you each go back to your lines.

ok.log: Brother against brother on the field. You win, and you wish you had not.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Red Sash in the Bag

events.text: {npc} is a small child and has just performed your best form perfectly after watching you once. A disciple in blue robes from a nearby sect saw it too.

effects.log: {He} goes up the mountain so young, with a bag bigger than {he} is. You watch until the path turns.
A child should be a child. The sect's recruiter says they will come back. They do.

events.text: {npc}'s first tournament. {He} is the youngest in the draw, and {he} has asked you not to come because you make {him} nervous.

choices.text: Go anyway, and hide in the crowd

effects.log: You watch from behind a pillar. {He} wins the first round and looks straight at the pillar.
You hear {he} reached the semi-final from a neighbour. {He} tells you in person a week later, over dinner, every exchange.

events.text: {npc} has surpassed you. {He} says so gently, in the training yard, after beating you three times in a row with a form you taught {him}.

effects.log: You bow to your own child. {He} bursts into tears, which rather spoils the moment.

ok.log: You lose the fourth round too. You are laughing by the end of it.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Child Who Watched Once

events.text: A stranger at the market calls your spouse by a name you have never heard. Your spouse goes pale and says the stranger is mistaken.

choices.text: Ask about the name that night

effects.log: The story comes out in pieces: another province, another family, a reason to leave that was not a crime but looked like one.
You decide a person is who they are now. It is a kind decision and a dangerous one.

events.text: A man with a sword at your gate at midnight, asking for your spouse by the old name. He is not here to talk.

ok.log: Steel in the dark, your family behind the door.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Other Name

choices.text: Let your spouse answer the door

effects.log: They talk for an hour in a language you do not know. The man leaves. Your spouse does not sleep for a week.

events.text: The whole truth, at last, on a winter night: the old name, the old family, what was done, and why your spouse ran. It is not what you feared. It is worse, and it is not your spouse's fault.

effects.log: Nothing else needs saying. The name is never spoken again in your house.

choices.text: Travel to the old province and set it right

effects.log: A journey of a season, a magistrate, a grave, and a very old wrong put right in a day.

events.text: The family shrine has been broken into. The tablets are untouched; the floor under them is open, and the box that was there is gone.

ok.log: Fresh prints to the river. A boat, and a long chase.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Box Under the Tablets

choices.text: Ask the oldest relative what was in the box

effects.log: 'Your great-grandfather's manual,' she says. 'The one he said was cursed. He was not joking.'

events.text: The manual comes back to you by a strange road: the robber dead in a ditch, the box beside him, every page intact and every page cold to the touch.

effects.log: Your great-grandfather's hand, a form nobody teaches any more, and a warning on the last page you read too late.

choices.text: Bury it under the shrine, deeper

effects.log: You dig for a day. The cold stays in your hands for a month.

events.text: Three patients in a morning with the same black-rimmed sores. By evening it is thirty. The town's other physicians are already packing.

choices.text: Stay and shut the town gates

effects.log: You persuade the magistrate to close the gates. The town hates you for a season and lives.

choices.text: Ride for the capital's medicine halls

effects.log: You bring back three physicians and a cart of herbs. The sores are gone by winter.

events.text: A cure, half-found: a root that stops the sores spreading but kills one patient in eight. You have two hundred patients and a week.

effects.log: Twenty-five graves and a hundred and seventy-five people who go home.
Three more days of searching, forty more sores, and then the proper cure, in a weed growing on the hall's own roof.

events.text: The province remembers. A plaque with your name on it goes up on the medicine hall, and a letter arrives from the court.

effects.log: An Imperial Physician's robe, and a very long way from your town.
The plaque is enough. The court sends the robe anyway.

events.text: The agency master gives you a sealed red chest to carry to the capital, a guard of six, and one instruction: do not open it, whatever happens.

effects.log: Six guards, one chest, forty days of road.

choices.text: Weigh it, shake it, listen to it

effects.log: Something inside shifts, slowly, and is still. You carry it anyway, further from your body.

events.text: Bandits on the pass, far too many, and far too interested in the red chest for ordinary bandits.

ok.log: You hold the pass with the chest at your back.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Red Chest

choices.text: Open the chest and see what you are dying for

effects.log: Inside, in straw, a sleeping child with a prince's birthmark. The bandits are not bandits. You run.

events.text: The capital. The chest is delivered, or the child is, and a man in a court robe hands you a pouch and tells you that you were never here.

effects.log: Gold enough to buy an agency of your own. You remember anyway.
The man tells you, very quietly, and then you really do wish you had taken the pouch and gone.

events.text: A sect disciple is dead in an inn room and another sect's disciple was seen leaving it. Both sects are at the court door by noon with their swords, and the case lands on your desk as the one official who knows the murim.

effects.log: Witnesses, the innkeeper, the room. It takes a week and both sects hate the delay.
The Alliance takes the case and the credit. Your court keeps its roof.

events.text: The evidence says the accused disciple did it. The accused disciple's sect says that if you say so aloud, there will be no court here by morning.

effects.log: You pass the sentence in a full court. The sect's elders look at you for a long moment and then, to everyone's surprise, bow.

choices.text: Find a way to make it an accident

effects.log: The court survives. You do not sleep well for a year.

events.text: The guild sends you west with forty camels of silk and a map with a great deal of sand on it.

effects.log: Forty days of sand.
The deputy comes back rich and does not speak to you again.

events.text: A sandstorm swallows the caravan for three days. When it clears you are somewhere that is not on the map, beside a city that is not on any map.

effects.log: They have never seen silk. They pay in a stone that glows.
You find the road again by the stars. You never find the city again.

events.text: Home, and rich, and the rival guild has heard about the glowing stones. They would like the map. They have hired people to ask.

ok.log: The guild hall, after dark.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Forty Camels West

choices.text: Sell them a map with a great deal of sand on it

effects.log: They go west. They do not come back for two years, and when they do, they are not rich.

events.text: A name on the black list with a price that would buy a house, and a rumour that nobody who has gone after it has come back.

effects.log: You take the poster from the board. The other hunters go quiet.
Three hunters take it. None of them come back. You learn a great deal from that.

variants: A name on the black list, with a price that would buy a house, and a whisper that nobody who went after it ever came back.

events.text: You find the name in a village in the hills, teaching children to read. {He} knows why you have come and asks only that you let {him} finish the lesson.

effects.log: The crime was real. So was the reason. The price was put on {him} by the man {he} wronged, who wronged a great many people first.

ok.log: A short fight. {He} does not try very hard.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Name in the Hills

events.text: The man who posted the price finds you, with guards, to ask why the name is still teaching children in the hills.

choices.text: Tell him the contract is void

ok.log: He does not take it well. Neither do his guards.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Name in the Hills

effects.log: You give back a down payment you never spent. He looks at you as if you were mad, which from his side you are.

choices.text: Stand there and let him rage

effects.log: He calls you every kind of coward and cheat, and you say nothing back. In the end he spits at your feet and rides away with his guards. The name in the hills goes on teaching.

events.arc: The Old Man in the Corner
events.text: The old man in the corner has drunk on credit for a year and the keeper wants him out. Tonight three swordsmen come in looking for him, and he is too drunk to stand.

ok.log: Three swordsmen in a tavern. The tables do not survive.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Old Man in the Corner

effects.log: The swordsmen take him into the street. You hear nothing. In the morning the street is clean and so is his tab.

events.arc: The Old Man in the Corner
events.text: The old man, sober for once, sits you down after closing and shows you a form with a wine cup that you have never seen and cannot believe exists.

effects.log: Every night after closing for a year, with a cup, in the dark.
He tells you a name. It is on the list of the Ten Greatest from long ago.

events.arc: The Old Man in the Corner
events.text: The old man does not come down one morning. On his table, a deed: the inn, bought years ago with silver nobody knew he had, left to the one person who stood in front of him.

effects.log: You are an innkeeper. The corner table is never sold.

choices.text: Sell it and build him a proper grave

effects.log: A stone with his real name on it, which makes the old fighters who pass through stop and stare.

events.text: {pet_name} comes home at dusk with a snare wire round one leg. Poachers have moved into the hills, and they take anything with a pelt.

ok.log: Wire, traps, and finally the men, at a camp fire.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Snare Wire

effects.log: A season at your side. {pet_name} sulks magnificently.

events.text: The poachers come for {pet_name} in the night, with nets. They have found that beasts who walk beside martial artists fetch a very high price.

ok.log: You and {pet_name}, back to back in the yard.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Snare Wire

effects.log: You open the gate. The nets are not enough. The poachers do not come back to this province.

events.text: Old now, grey with age, {pet_name} lies by your door and does not get up when you call, and looks at you as if to say: I would if I could.

effects.log: A long afternoon. The light goes gold and then grey.

choices.text: Carry {pet_name} to the hill above the house

effects.log: Heavier than before. The view is good. {pet_name} watches it until the watching stops.

events.text: The town's autumn race is open to any horse, and the merchants' sons have already laughed at yours.

effects.log: {pet_name} runs as if insulted, which is fair.

choices.text: Hire your horse out to a rider instead

effects.log: A nervous young rider takes {pet_name} round the course and wins by a length. You keep the hire and half the purse.

events.text: The merchants' sons have fixed next year's race: a loose shoe, a bribed starter, a rider with a hidden spike. A stable boy tells you for a copper.

choices.text: Race anyway, and watch for the spike

effects.log: {pet_name} shies at the right moment. The spiked rider goes into the ditch. You win by a length.

choices.text: Bring the stable boy to the magistrate

effects.log: The race is cancelled and the merchants' sons spend the autumn in a cell. {pet_name} is bored.

events.text: {pet_name} wakes you before dawn and will not be calmed. Something is calling from the mountains, and {pet_name} wants you to come.

effects.log: Three days into mountains you have never seen on a map.
{pet_name} stays, for you, and for a year looks at the mountains every dusk.

events.text: A valley of {pet_name}'s own kind, who look at you the way you would look at a dog's pet. Their eldest sets you a trial: a night alone on the peak, unarmed.

effects.log: Cold, wind, and something that circles you all night and never quite strikes.

choices.text: Refuse: you are not theirs to test

effects.log: The eldest laughs, a sound like a landslide. {pet_name} chooses to go home with you. The valley does not object.

events.text: An envoy in court silk at your furnace: the Emperor's mother is dying, and the court has heard of your pills.

effects.log: A list of ingredients, half of which you have never seen.

choices.text: Decline: a failure would cost your head

effects.log: The envoy nods as if he expected it. He takes the list to someone braver, or more foolish.

events.text: The last ingredient grows on one cliff in the far west and is guarded by a hermit who has spent sixty years making sure it is never picked.

ok.log: An old man with a hoe who fights like a Peak Master. He is one.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Emperor's Mother

choices.text: Sit with him until he gives it to you

effects.log: Forty days of tea on the cliff. On the forty-first he hands you the flower and tells you he had been waiting sixty years for someone patient.

events.text: The pill, in your hand, in the throne room, the whole court watching you walk the long carpet.

effects.log: The Emperor's mother lives another nine years. You are allowed to leave the capital, which is rarer than it sounds.

choices.text: Present it, and ask for one thing

effects.log: You ask for the hermit's cliff to be made a protected mountain. The court laughs, and then the Emperor's mother says yes.

events.text: A stranger with a heavy purse wants a blade forged with no maker's mark, no questions, and a promise not to ask.

effects.log: Your best work, nameless. The silver is very good.
The stranger shrugs and goes to a worse smith. The blade still gets made.

events.text: A friend of yours is dead on the Luoyang road, and the wound was made by a blade that was obviously, unmistakably yours.

ok.log: The purse was heavy. So is your hammer.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Blade Without a Mark

choices.text: Swear an oath: a mark on every blade from now on

effects.log: You cut your mark into the anvil. No blade leaves without it again.

events.text: The nameless blade comes back to you, years later, in the hands of a child who found it in a river and wants to know whose it was.

effects.log: All of it. The child listens, and then asks you to teach them to forge. You do.

choices.text: Melt it in front of them

effects.log: The steel runs. You make the child a small plain knife from it, with your mark.

events.text: A manor in the hills where nobody sleeps. The owner has tried monks, Taoists and a very loud drum. He has heard that you lay arrays.

effects.log: Cold spots that move. A door that is never where it was. Footsteps on a floor above the roof.

choices.text: Lay a Guardian Array at every door

effects.log: The arrays hold. Whatever it is cannot leave either, which the owner had not considered.

events.text: The thing in the manor is not a ghost. It is a very old array in the foundations, still running, still guarding a room that no longer exists against a thief who died three hundred years ago.

effects.log: Three nights of chalk and candles. On the fourth the house is just a house.
You copy every line. It is a Heaven-Locking Array laid by a master. You learn more in a week than in ten years.

events.text: A monk with skin like old bronze stops at your gate and asks, politely, whether the body tempering you practise is real or something you tell people.

ok.log: You let him hit you. Then he lets you hit him. Neither of you is happy with the result.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Bronze Monk

effects.log: He drinks nine cups and tells you about a waterfall in the north where the monks temper their bodies under ice.

events.text: The northern falls, in winter, with the bronze monk sitting under the ice as if it were a warm bath, waving you in.

effects.log: Your heart stops for a moment. Then it starts again, differently.

choices.text: Sit on the bank and watch

effects.log: You watch for a season. On the last day you go in, for a breath. It counts.

events.text: Your cellmate has been inside for eleven years and has a plan with a drawing on the wall and a loose stone for every year.

effects.log: You spend your nights widening a stone's gap with a spoon.
The plan goes on without you. So does the spoon.

events.text: The night. The stones come out, the drain is where the drawing said, and your cellmate goes first. Then the alarm, and your cellmate's face in the drain mouth, deciding.

choices.text: Push your cellmate through and face the guards

effects.log: Your cellmate goes. You do not. Three more years, and a letter every spring from someone free.
You are out. Your cellmate is caught in the drain behind you, and laughs, which you will never understand.

events.text: A tavern years later, and your old cellmate at a table with a glass raised to you before you have seen who it is.

effects.log: You talk until dawn about the drain and the spoon. Your old cellmate pays, a merchant now.

choices.text: Leave before a word is said

effects.log: Some debts are easier unpaid. You think about the drain for a year.

events.text: A village that asks no questions, a room over a stable, and a widow who feeds you and does not look at the posters in the market.

effects.log: You mend her roof and her fence. It is the quietest season of your life.
The road again. You leave silver on the table.

events.text: The widow's brother has seen the poster and worked out the sum. Constables on the road at dawn, and the widow at your door at midnight to tell you so.

choices.text: Stand with the widow against the brother

ok.log: A family quarrel in a stable yard, and a brother who leaves with a broken nose and no silver.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Widow's Stable

effects.log: You are gone before the constables. You never learn what happened to her for it.

events.text: The Pavilion's contract comes on black paper as always: a name, a house, a night. The name is nine years old.

effects.log: You send the paper back blank. Nobody refuses the Pavilion.

choices.text: Take the contract and warn the house

effects.log: You take the Pavilion's silver and spend the night on the child's roof, blade out, facing the other way.

events.text: The Pavilion sends two Night Blades to explain why nobody refuses. They find you at the child's house, which was their second guess.

ok.log: Two of the Pavilion's best, in a courtyard, with a child asleep upstairs.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Contract on Black Paper

choices.text: Hand them the Pavilion's own silver and the name of who bought the contract

effects.log: They look at the name, and at each other, and leave. The Pavilion has rules about buyers, too.

choices.text: Carry the child out the back while they search

effects.log: Over the back wall with the child asleep on your shoulder, and three cold days in the hills. The Night Blades go home empty-handed. The Pavilion strikes your name from its rolls, which is better than the other thing it does.

events.text: The child, grown, at your gate with a sword and a question: why.

effects.log: They listen. Then they kneel, which you had not expected and do not want.

choices.text: Tell them to put the sword down first

effects.log: They do. Then you tell them. Then you teach them, because somebody should.

events.arc: The Dice Under the Silk Shop
events.text: The den under the silk shop has a table where the dice fall your way for an hour, and then a very long night where they do not.

choices.text: Walk away while you are up

effects.log: You leave with silver and your dignity, which the den finds unsporting.
The dice know. By dawn you owe the den a house you do not have.

events.arc: The Dice Under the Silk Shop
events.text: The den's enforcer, a man built like a wardrobe, comes to collect what you owe or the fingers you would otherwise use to roll.

ok.log: A wardrobe with fists.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Dice Under the Silk Shop

choices.text: Offer to work it off at the table

effects.log: You run the dice for a year. You learn how they fall your way for an hour.

events.arc: The Dice Under the Silk Shop
events.text: The den's owner dies with no heir and a drawer full of debts, yours among them, and the enforcer suggests, awkwardly, that someone who knows the dice should take the place.

effects.log: You own a gambling den. You make the dice honest, and lose money for a year, and then do not.

choices.text: Burn the drawer and walk out

effects.log: Every debt in town goes up in smoke, including yours. The town buys you dinner for a decade.

events.text: A flute from the next courtyard every evening, playing one tune badly. On the ninth evening you answer it, worse.

effects.log: A duet of two bad players, every evening for a season. Then a note over the wall.
A startled face, a dropped flute, and the start of something.

events.text: The parents of {npc}, the flute player, have found the notes. They have also found a better match, in another province, leaving within the month.

effects.log: A horse, a night, and a wedding in a village temple with a monk who asks no questions.

choices.text: Let them go, as the parents ask

effects.log: The flute stops. Years later you hear it again, in the capital, played very well, and do not go to see who.

events.text: {npc} has taken vows your sect does not allow to be broken, and you are both standing in a moonlit courtyard not breaking them, very carefully.

effects.log: You say it. {He} does not say it back. {He} does not leave either.
Years of saying nothing in moonlit courtyards. It is a kind of vow too.

events.text: An elder saw you and {npc}. The two of you are called before the hall: renounce, or leave the mountain.

effects.log: Two robes left folded on a step. A long road.
You say the words. {He} says them too. You pass each other in the courtyard for the rest of your lives.

events.text: The innkeeper at the crossroads lost a spouse to a bandit's blade three years ago and runs the place alone, better than the spouse did. You find yourself stopping there more than the road requires.

choices.text: Stay a season and mend the roof

effects.log: The roof did not need mending. You both know it.
The innkeeper tells you a name and a stronghold, and does not ask you to do anything about it.

events.text: The bandit who killed the innkeeper's spouse is drinking in her inn, laughing, with eight men, not knowing whose wine it is.

ok.log: Eight men and the one who matters. The tables do not survive. The inn does.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Inn at the Crossroads

choices.text: Pour his wine yourself and tell him whose inn this is

effects.log: He goes very quiet and leaves silver on the table enough for ten dinners. It is not enough. It is something.

events.text: Spring at the crossroads, the roof mended, and {npc}, the innkeeper, asking, without looking up from the ledger, whether you intend to keep stopping here.

effects.log: You keep stopping here. Then you stop leaving.

choices.text: Say the road is your life

effects.log: {npc} nods at the ledger. You stop at the inn for years to come and never once stay the winter.

events.text: Your family has arranged a match with {npc}, of a great house of the north. You have seen a portrait. The portrait has seen you.

effects.log: A wedding with two hundred guests and {npc}, whom you have spoken to twice.
A chaperoned garden, a stiff hour, and then a joke that neither of you expected the other to make.

events.text: {npc} has a secret, told to you under a plum tree: there is someone else, in the north, and the match was arranged to end it.

effects.log: A horse at midnight and a letter to your family that costs you a year of silence from your father.
A marriage of two friends who both know. It lasts longer than most of the other kind.

events.text: A storm drives you into a cave on the mountain, and the back of the cave is a door, and the door is open.

effects.log: A chamber, a skeleton in robes, and on its lap a manual that has waited a very long time.

choices.text: Wait out the storm at the mouth

effects.log: You sleep by the fire. In the morning the door is a wall.

events.text: A sect you have never heard of has heard of the cave. Three of them wait at your gate, polite, patient, and very much wanting the manual that their founder died beside.

effects.log: They bow to the ground. They leave a jade token and a standing invitation.

ok.log: They bow less deeply. They do not leave.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Door in the Cave

events.text: The skeleton's sect, years later, is dying out. Their last elder comes to ask the one who found their founder's manual to carry it on, however you got it.

choices.text: Take their last disciple as your own

effects.log: A sect of two, and a manual from a cave. It is enough to begin with.

choices.text: Teach the elder your own forms in exchange

effects.log: An old man learning new forms in your yard. Both sects come out of it changed.

events.text: A monk at the market looks at you for a long moment and says you will die three times and live four, and will not take a coin for saying it.

effects.log: He smiles and buys you a bun. 'You will know the third time.'
He laughs too. He has very good teeth for a monk.

events.text: A blade you did not see, a wound that should have killed you, and a physician who says you were dead for the length of a breath. The first time.

effects.log: You count. One.
Luck, then. You are more careful on the road after.

events.text: The second time: qi deviation, your meridians on fire, and a voice in the dark that says 'not yet' in the monk's exact tone.

effects.log: You come back. Two.
You come back anyway. The voice sounds amused.

events.text: The monk, unchanged in all these years, at the market again, with a bun. 'The third time,' he says, 'is the one you choose.'

effects.log: He does. It takes all afternoon and you understand about half. The half is enough.

choices.text: Buy him a bun this time

effects.log: He accepts with great dignity. 'Four,' he says, and is gone when you look up.

events.text: The gates of the underworld stand open for the ghost month, and a friend who died years ago is sitting at your table as if nothing had happened, asking for wine.

effects.log: You pour for the dead and sit with them, over tea, until the candle gutters. Your friend has a favour to ask.
Your friend is gone. You are not sure anyone was ever there, except for the two cups.

events.text: The favour: a grave in the hills, unmarked, dug too shallow by people in a hurry, and a name that was never cut into stone.

choices.text: Find the grave and cut the name

effects.log: Two days of searching, a day of stone. The hills are quieter after.

choices.text: Find who was in a hurry

ok.log: A name leads to a stronghold. The stronghold leads to a fight.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of A Cup for the Dead

events.arc: An Old Grudge, a New Sword
events.text: A youth at your gate with a new sword and an old grudge: you beat {his} master once, decades ago, and {he} has come to settle it.

ok.log: The yard, the youth, and a form you recognise with a pang.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of An Old Grudge, a New Sword

choices.text: Invite {him} to train with you for a year first

effects.log: {He} refuses, then accepts, then stays three years.

events.arc: An Old Grudge, a New Sword
events.text: The youth, no longer a youth, has made a name, and the storytellers say {he} learned it all from you, which is not true and which {he} never corrects.

effects.log: A legend with your name in it. It will outlive you both.

choices.text: Write the truth to the storytellers

effects.log: They ignore the letter. The story is better.

events.text: A rumour among the Transcendent: a gate, somewhere beyond the western mountains, that opens once in a generation to those who have gone as far as a body can go.

effects.log: A journey of a year, west and then further west.
Rumours. You have a life here.

events.text: Beyond the last mountain, a wall of mist, and a voice in it that knows your name and every life you have lived.

effects.log: The mist takes your memories out one at a time and holds them up to the light.
You turn. The voice says 'later', not unkindly.

events.text: The mist thins and there is a gate, plain wood, slightly open, and nothing at all visible beyond it except light.

effects.log: You walk through the Last Door and do not come back. The world will remember.

fail.deathCause: the gate beyond the mist

choices.text: Sit down in front of it

effects.log: You sit by the gate for a year and then go home, and live a very long time, and never tell anyone what you saw.

events.text: The sect's treasury is light by two hundred taels and the elder who keeps it has started wearing a new ring.

effects.log: The master thanks you and does nothing, visibly. The ring vanishes. So does the elder's smile when he sees you.

choices.text: Follow the elder on his trips to town

effects.log: He visits a gambling house. He loses. He is not stealing for himself.

events.text: The elder's son owes the gambling house his life, and the elder has been paying it in the sect's silver. The son is standing in front of you with a knife.

effects.log: A boy with a knife is not a fight. You sit him down and hear it all.

choices.text: Bring both of them to the hall

effects.log: The council hears it. The elder loses his seat and keeps his son.

events.text: The gambling house would like its silver, and has sent a dozen men up the mountain to collect it from a sect that owes it nothing.

ok.log: A dozen collectors against the whole sect. It is not long.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Elder's New Ring

choices.text: Pay the debt from your own purse and end it

effects.log: Two hundred taels, and the elder's son free. He becomes an outer disciple the next spring.

choices.text: Bar the gate and leave it to the elders

effects.log: You bar the gate and send for the elders. The collectors shout at the walls until dark, then go back down the mountain. The sect remembers that you did not step forward.

events.text: A Cult envoy walks into your sect's hall under a white flag, alone, with a proposal: a year's truce on the western roads, in exchange for the return of a captured Black Robe.

effects.log: The elders argue for a day. The truce holds for the year. The roads are quiet.
The envoy leaves without the Black Robe. The western roads burn by autumn.

events.text: The year is over. The envoy is back, with the same white flag and a different proposal: {he} would like to defect, and {he} has asked for you by name.

effects.log: {He} lives in the outer halls under guard for ten years, then under none. {He} never once gives you reason to regret it.
{He} leaves under the white flag. A year later {his} head is on the Cult's gate. It was not a trick.

events.text: The rains fail and the village below the mountain eats its seed grain. The children stop playing in the lane.

effects.log: You open the store. The elders are furious for a season and proud for a decade.
Every day in the hills, every evening a deer or nothing.

events.text: Bandits hear of a village that still has food. Forty of them, hungry too, which makes them worse.

ok.log: Forty hungry men and one lane.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Seed Grain

choices.text: Share the village's food with the bandits

effects.log: You walk out with a sack. Half of them put down their weapons and pick up hoes by spring.

events.text: In a golden age the sects compete with tournaments instead of wars, and this year's is the grandest in living memory, with the Emperor's own brother in the stands.

ok.log: The grand draw. Your name is called to a roar.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Grandest Tournament

effects.log: You see every bout and learn a form from each. The Emperor's brother nods to you once, for no reason you can tell.

events.text: The Emperor's brother sends for the fighter he noticed. He would like a teacher for his sons. The pay is the sort of number people whisper.

effects.log: Three years in the capital, three boys who hate you and then do not.
He is amused. Nobody declines. He sends you a horse to make up for it.

events.text: The Iron Decree is nailed to the city gate: no martial arts within the walls. Eastern Depot agents watch the training yards with ledgers.

choices.text: Train in secret, at night, in a warehouse

effects.log: Thirty people in a warehouse with wrapped blades. It is the best training yard you ever had.

choices.text: Leave the city for the hills

effects.log: You train on a hilltop with the city below. The Depot does not climb hills.

events.text: The warehouse is raided. Depot agents at every door and a ledger with your name in it.

ok.log: Agents in the dark among the barrels.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Warehouse School

effects.log: Two years in a prefecture cell, with your name in the Depot ledger.

events.text: A disciple you trained, {npc}, has not come back from a mission. The sect writes {him} off. You do not.

effects.log: A cold trail across two provinces.
You light one every night for a year. On the last night someone knocks.

events.text: {npc}, alive, thinner, with a story of a bandit cell and a year of chains, and a question: did anyone come?

effects.log: 'You did,' {he} says, and that is all {he} ever says about it.
A kind lie. {He} believes it for a year, and then does not, and forgives you anyway.

events.text: The sect's matchmaker, an elder with a ledger of every unmarried disciple on the mountain, has found you a match in a rival sect: an alliance by marriage.

effects.log: A tea ceremony between two sects' elders and two very embarrassed disciples.
The elder crosses you out with great ceremony. You are free, and slightly insulted.

events.text: {npc}, the match, turns out to be as unwilling as you were, and suggests over the fourth cup of tea that the two of you fake a terrible quarrel to end it.

effects.log: A magnificent quarrel in the courtyard. The elders despair. You and {npc} become fast friends.
A long silence over the fifth cup. Then a wedding both sects claim as their idea.

events.text: A temple on a peak nobody climbs, a bell that rings by itself at dawn, and an old monk who asks you to carry water up for a season in exchange for nothing he will name.

effects.log: Ninety mornings of stairs. On the ninety-first the monk is gone and the bell rings for you.
'Strong legs,' says the monk, and sends you down the mountain.

events.text: The temple, years later, with a new monk in it, very young, who says the old one left a scroll for 'the one who carried water'.

effects.log: A breathing method written in a hand that shakes with age or laughter.

choices.text: Leave it for the next one

effects.log: The young monk looks at you as if you were mad. You feel lighter walking down.

events.text: The northern garrison is short of swords and the steppe riders are not short of horses. A captain at the inn asks for anyone who can hold a wall for a month.

ok.log: A month of cold, arrows, and a wall that holds.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of The Eastern Wall

choices.text: Sell the garrison your sword and go home

effects.log: A good sword, a fair price, and a captain who looks at you with contempt.

events.text: A rider from the steppe under a truce flag, asking for the one who held the eastern wall: {his} brother fell there, and {he} would like to know how.

effects.log: A brave death, you say, and it is true. {He} leaves a horse tied to the gate in the morning.

choices.text: Refuse to speak to the enemy

effects.log: {He} rides away. The next spring the raids are worse on your stretch of wall.

events.text: Black sails off the coast and a fishing village with every boat burned. The pirates will be back for the rest when the tide turns.

choices.text: Hide in the boats and wait for them

ok.log: A night in a fish hold with a drawn blade and a very bad smell.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Black Sails

effects.log: Three hundred people on a hill road by dawn. The pirates burn empty houses.

events.text: The pirate captain, caught or not, has a bounty posted by the coastal prefect that would buy you a boat of your own.

choices.text: Take a boat out after the black sails

ok.log: Three days at sea, and a fight on a rolling deck.

fail.log: You lose, and spend a season on your bruises.
fail.deathCause: a gamble that failed in the tale of Black Sails

effects.log: A season of planing wood. The village names a boat after you, which is a kind of bounty.
